findings.title: Starting the resource watcher after index initialization can drop events
findings.body: `search.init` can take a long time, but the resource watcher is now started only after it completes. `WatchWriteEvents` begins polling from the latest resource version when it is opened, so writes made by other server instances during index construction are not replayed to this server's watch stream. Clients reconnecting with a `Since` version from before startup can therefore miss changes. Start the resource watcher before the long index build, or ensure the watcher replays from a durable cursor.

findings.title: Concurrent index builds can race with TotalDocs map iteration
findings.body: `BuildIndex` now permits concurrent builds and writes to `b.cache` under `cacheMu`, but `TotalDocs` iterates the same map without taking that lock. If a build overlaps `TotalDocs`, Go can report a concurrent map iteration/write and crash the process. This can occur during startup if a watch event triggers an index build after the watch starts but before the initialization log calls `TotalDocs`. Protect the iteration with the same lock or otherwise snapshot the cache safely.

findings.title: Initialization failure returns without cleaning up initialized resources
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now runs `Init` before returning, but on an error it returns `nil` without stopping the lifecycle hooks or canceling the server context. If lifecycle initialization has opened resources, or search initialization has started its background watcher before a later initialization step fails, there is no returned server for the caller to stop and those resources can leak. Clean up partially initialized components before returning the error.
